content.text: Have you ever noticed how a straw in a glass of water appears bent? Or how pools look shallower than they really are? These effects are caused by refraction—the bending of waves as they pass from one medium to another. Understanding refraction explains many optical phenomena and is crucial for designing lenses and optical instruments.
is the change in direction of a wave when it passes from one medium to another, caused by a change in wave speed.
Occurs at the boundary between two media
Wave changes speed in the new medium
If entering at an angle, the wave changes direction
When a wave enters a new medium:
Wave speed changes (depends on the medium)
Frequency stays the same (set by the source)
If entering at an angle, one side of the wavefront slows before the other
This causes the wave to bend
Wave after passing into new medium
Angle between incident ray and normal
Angle between refracted ray and normal

content.text: When Light Hits Perpendicular to Surface

When light enters a denser medium it slows down and bends towards the normal. When it enters a less dense medium it speeds up and bends away from the normal. If it hits perpendicular to the boundary, it slows or speeds up but does not change direction.
of a material indicates how much light slows down in that material.
$$n = \frac{c}{v} = \frac{\text{speed of light in vacuum}}{\text{speed of light in medium}}$$
Higher refractive index = slower light = more bending

Total internal reflection only occurs when light travels from a denser to a less dense medium AND the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle. It cannot happen when light enters a denser medium.
Light travels from water (n = 1.33) to air (n = 1.0). The angle in water is 30°. Find the angle in air.
(Light bends away from normal when entering less dense medium)
When light travels from a denser medium to a less dense medium at a large enough angle, ALL the light is reflected back—none passes through.

Different wavelengths (colours) refract by slightly different amounts:
"Light always bends when entering a new medium"
— Only if entering at an angle. Perpendicular rays don't bend.
"Total internal reflection happens at any angle"
— Only at angles greater than the critical angle, and only when going from denser to less dense medium.
— Frequency stays constant. Wavelength and speed change.
— It's the opposite! Higher n means slower light.
— All waves refract, including sound and water waves.

Refraction is bending of waves due to change in speed at a boundary
Light bends toward normal when entering denser medium (slows down)
Light bends away from normal when entering less dense medium (speeds up)
Frequency constant; wavelength and speed change
Applications: optical fibres, prisms, lenses, diamond sparkle
